instruction: Repair the rotation functionality in my Tetris game. Modify tetris.py so that rotate() checks for collisions and only applies rotation if valid.

metadata.explanation: AST-based verification that rotate() method contains conditional statements and method calls for collision checking.
metadata.bug_description: The rotate() method in tetris.py doesn't check for collision after rotation, causing crashes when blocks are near boundaries.
metadata.expected_fix: Add old_rotation = self.block.rotation before rotating, call self.intersect() after rotation, and restore self.block.rotation = old_rotation if intersection is detected.

llm_judge_reasons: Strong verification of core requirements: Metric comprehensively checks for old_rotation save, rotation modification, intersect() call, and conditional restoration pattern
Conditional restoration logic is well-verified: Checks that if statement condition calls intersect() AND body restores self.block.rotation to old_rotation (lines 88-112)
Sequence verification present: Ensures old_rotation is saved before rotation is modified (lines 115-117)
Complete coverage of instruction requirements: All aspects of the fix are checked - save state, check collision, restore if needed

Minor sequencing gap: Doesn't strictly verify intersect() is called AFTER rotation modification, only that it exists. However, the conditional restoration pattern strongly implies correct implementation
Getter logic is straightforward: Simple file reading from VM, should work correctly at runtime
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add verification that intersect() call occurs AFTER rotation modification in statement sequence (not just anywhere in the method)
Consider adding position tracking to ensure the intersect() call happens between rotation and conditional restoration
Could strengthen by verifying intersect() is called specifically on the rotated state (though current conditional check mostly ensures this)
